notes:
This is an early build, released to consoles set to Latest Updates.

PC games, controllers: each game's Controllers screen has a Controller row.
Gamepad lets the game read your controller as before. Keyboard and mouse is for
games without controller support: the game sees no controller at all, the right
stick moves the mouse, and the buttons press keys. The bottom button left
clicks, the right button is Backspace, Plus is Enter, Minus is Esc, the left
button right clicks, the top button is Space, the left stick is WASD, the d-pad
is the arrow keys, L and R are Q and E, ZL and ZR right and left click, and the
stick clicks are Shift and Ctrl. Remap on a controller changes any of them. A
game that had Keyboard on the controller turned on is now set to Keyboard and
mouse.

The Capture button can turn the right-stick mouse on and off (the default),
press any key or mouse button, open the on-screen keyboard, or do nothing: pick
one on the Remap screen. The pause menu's Mouse on the right stick row is gone,
since Capture does that now.

The on-screen keyboard no longer pauses the game, and each key goes into the
game as you press it. It has Backspace, Enter and arrow keys, Plus is Enter,
and Close or B puts it away. Handheld, you can tap its keys. Besides the pause
menu, Capture or a touch button can open it, and so can any button in Keyboard
and mouse mode. Each key is held a little longer, so a game that reads the
keyboard once a frame sees it.

Touch buttons: handheld, a PC game can show up to ten buttons on the screen,
down the sides or along the top or bottom. Each presses a key or mouse button,
or opens the keyboard, with a label you type. A small Hide button tucks them
away, a touch anywhere else is still the mouse, and the pause menu can change
them during the game, along with how solid the labels' backgrounds are.

Steam downloads on the web page can go to the Linux partition, which has no
4 GB limit per file, as well as to the SD card.

Fixed: a key held when you opened the pause menu, such as walking forward with
the left stick, no longer stays held after you close it.

The touch buttons and keyboard were tested with a simulated touch panel rather
than a finger, and Keyboard and mouse mode in game menus, not full gameplay or
Steam games.

stable.notes:
The 2.41 changes, now on the Stable channel. If this console was on 2.40.0,
it also gets the whole 2.40 series, summed up at the end.

This update carries a new boot script: the console restarts once for the
update and once more on its own about a minute after the first boot. Do not
power off while it says part 2 of 2.

The SD card's fastest mode (DDR200) is now used on Samsung cards only, as
Switchroot does. Other cards run in the standard mode: if yours used the
fast mode, games load a little slower, but SanDisk cards, which cannot run
it reliably on the Switch, no longer get read errors under load. If a
Samsung card gives read errors, turn DDR200 off in the SCCM Retro app's Boot
settings.

The SCCM Retro app on the Homebrew menu is now one app: Launch SCCM Retro,
Launch in Safe Mode (stock clocks and voltages, once), Options (WiFi and
Bluetooth, boot settings, auto launch), and installing or removing SCCM
Retro on an SD card. The separate installer and calibration apps are
removed.

Swap A and B now applies only to Gen1Recomp and Moonlight, the two games
that offer it.

New background: Arcade, in Settings, Display and Sound, Appearance.

From 2.40.0, also: the console boots in about 28 seconds instead of about
50; Ocarina of Time and Majora's Mask, and Mario Kart Wii as a native port
with Retro Rewind online, on Ports and Apps; a PC Games tab for Windows
games; auto save for RetroArch, 3DS and PS2 games; Wii U, GameCube, WiFi
and volume button fixes; and a security fix to install permissions.
